We are a team of passionate aerospace and technology enthusiasts interested in space exploration, innovation, and problem-solving. We aim to combine engineering, science, and technology to develop creative solutions for real-world challenges.

We are looking for motivated individuals with interests or skills in Python, software development, web development, UI/UX design, GIS mapping, 3D visualization, data science, AI/ML, and planetary science.
summary:
MarsWalk Planner is an integrated mission planning system designed to reduce risks for astronauts conducting Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) on the Martian surface. We developed an end-to-end telemetry pipeline and interactive visual interface. The system ingests Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and environmental datasets (radiation, thermal) and processes them through a custom Multi-Layer Cost Fusion engine, applying strict physiological constraints—such as limiting safe slopes to under 15 degrees. A core A* pathfinding algorithm uses this consolidated cost matrix to calculate the safest, most efficient route.

The resulting plan is visualized in a localized, dark-mode Mission Control interface with interactive layer toggles and real-time readouts, including projected EVA duration, suit oxygen utilization, and total mSv radiation dose. This is critical for crewed Mars exploration, where topographic instability and radiation exposure present severe safety challenges. MarsWalk Planner addresses these challenges by empowering planners with immediate, science-grounded, and customizable terrain risk assessment and optimized routing.

1. What does it do, and how does it work?

MarsWalk Planner is an end-to-end mission planning and navigation system for Martian extravehicular activities (EVAs).

  • The Backend Pipeline: It ingests elevation and environmental data (such as Digital Elevation Models, thermal inertia, and radiation flux) into a 2D grid structure. It calculates surface elevation gradients using NumPy (np.gradient), converts them into slope angles in degrees (θ=arctan⁡(dx2+dy2)\theta = \arctan(\sqrt{dx^2 + dy^2})θ=arctan(dx2+dy2

  • Cost Fusion & Pathfinding: It merges multiple environmental layers through a weighted summation formula(Ctotal=(w1.slope cost)+(w2.Radiation Cost)). A core A pathfinding algorithm* processes this consolidated cost matrix to calculate the safest, most efficient traverse route.
  • The Frontend Handoff: The path and telemetry are serialized into JSON (route.json) and handed off to an interactive, dark-mode Mission Control web interface.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Automated Risk Mitigation: Automatically detects and routes around life-threatening hazards like extreme grades and radiation hot spots.
  • Real-Time Telemetry Readouts: Instantly computes and displays crucial mission metrics, including total distance, estimated EVA duration, suit oxygen consumption, and cumulative radiation dosage (mSv\text{mSv}mSv).
  • Seamless Full-Stack Integration: Bridges advanced geospatial backend analytics with a user-friendly, interactive frontend map viewer complete with layer toggles and alternative route comparisons.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to enhance astronaut safety and mission success during future crewed surface operations on Mars. By providing planners with an immediate, science-grounded tool to visualize terrain risks and optimize EVA routes, MarsWalk Planner minimizes human error, reduces radiation exposure, and serves as a scalable concept demonstrator for planetary exploration software.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: Python (for backend data processing, cost matrix math, and pathfinding logic) and JavaScript/HTML/CSS (for the frontend mapping interface).
  • Libraries & Frameworks: NumPy (for high-performance 2D array operations and gradient calculations), Leaflet.js (for interactive map rendering and coordinate overlays).
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code (VS Code), Git, and custom simulation datasets modeled after real Martian topography (e.g., Gale Crater sub-grids and NASA Mars Trek tiles).

5. How is your project creative?

MarsWalk Planner creatively bridges the gap between raw planetary science data and actionable human operations. Instead of treating pathfinding as a purely abstract math problem, it fuses multiple physical layers—slope mechanics, radiation exposure, and spatial boundaries—into a unified cost function. Furthermore, wrapping this complex scientific pipeline into a sleek, functional Mission Control interface gives it the polish and usability of a real aerospace deployment tool.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Human Physiology & Safety Limits: Factoring in astronaut physical constraints, such as a maximum safe slope threshold (≤15∘\le 15^\circ≤15∘) and cumulative radiation limits (mSv\text{mSv}mSv).
  • Topographical Reality: Accounting for severe Martian hazards like cliff drop-offs by utilizing mathematical barriers (np.inf) that force absolute avoidance
  • System Modularity & Handoff: Designing clean interfaces between the science/data lead, the backend engineering pipeline, and the frontend developer via serialized JSON telemetry hand-offs.
